necessary_context.content: Minimize F(x)=f(x)+g(x) over R^n with Euclidean norm. g:R^n→R is continuous convex, possibly nonsmooth; f:R^n→R is convex and continuously differentiable with globally Lipschitz gradient, constant L(f)>0. X*=argmin F is nonempty, and F*=F(x*) for any x* in X*.
necessary_context.name: Problem and standing assumptions

necessary_context.content: For L>0, Q_L(x,y)=f(y)+<x−y,∇f(y)>+(L/2)||x−y||²+g(x); p_L(y)=argmin_x Q_L(x,y), uniquely defined. Equivalently p_L(y)=argmin_x {g(x)+(L/2)||x−(y−∇f(y)/L)||²}.
necessary_context.name: Quadratic model and exact proximal minimizer

necessary_context.content: If F(p_L(y))≤Q_L(p_L(y),y), then for every x in R^n, F(x)−F(p_L(y))≥(L/2)||p_L(y)−y||²+L<y−x,p_L(y)−y>. Lemma 2.1 ensures the premise for L at least a gradient Lipschitz constant; Lemma 2.2 supplies the exact subgradient optimality condition.
necessary_context.name: Basic inequality used by the proof
